This book is a 14-chapter course in statistical machine learning. It is
organized as a single concise sequence that combines concepts,
reproducible examples, and guided analysis.

The course is organized around a practical sequence:

1. Build statistical learning intuition from prediction, inference, and
   model error.
2. Use linear models as the first complete workflow for estimation,
   interpretation, diagnostics, and generalization.
3. Move from model assessment to resampling, feature engineering,
   regularization, nonlinear regression, classification, trees,
   ensembles, support vector machines, and unsupervised learning.
4. End with reproducible model development and the judgment needed to
   teach or deploy statistical learning responsibly.

| 5 | [Model Selection and Regularization](lectures/05-model-selection-regularization.qmd) |
| 6 | [Dimension Reduction](lectures/06-dimension-reduction.qmd) |

## Course Voice

The chapters use neutral course language rather than references to a
specific university, term, or software stack. Each chapter emphasizes
concepts, reproducible code, and statistical judgment.
